name: run-error-first-fails-the-run
description: a stream may OPEN with RUN_ERROR — the spec admits it, because a run can fail before it begins — so the client raises no first-event violation; and the failure the producer reported surfaces to the caller as a failed run rather than as a resolved one
kill: narrow the first-event check in verifyEvents (`eventType !== RUN_STARTED && eventType !== RUN_ERROR`) to RUN_STARTED alone — the leading RUN_ERROR then fails with `First event must be 'RUN_STARTED'` instead of the producer's own message, and `errorContains` fails. Removing the failure from the RUN_ERROR case in the reducer kills it the other way, leaving the run completed

dotnet.intentional: The .NET client has no reducer stage that can fail a run: EventStreamConverter reports RUN_ERROR as an ErrorContent update and the enumeration completes, so the stream is consumed successfully and the failure is observable only through `runError` (asserted above, unchanged). `errorContains` is deliberately the empty string, which asserts nothing — it LIFTS the base's requirement rather than restating it, because this lane produces no rejection to match against. Closing this divergence means giving the .NET client a way to surface a reported run failure as a failed consumption, and deleting this override.
